articles.title: Hubble reveals a stunning twist in how the universe emerged from darkness
articles.description: A surprising discovery by astronomers using the Hubble Space Telescope is challenging a leading explanation for how the early universe emerged from a dense fog of hydrogen roughly 13 billion years ago. Scientists once believed powerful winds from exploding stars helped radiation escape galaxies and clear that cosmic fog, but new observations reveal that these winds actually block radiation instead.
articles.summary: The Hubble Space Telescope has made a surprising discovery that challenges current understanding of how the universe emerged from darkness, potentially reshaping our cosmological models.

articles.title: Rubin Observatory Spots Possible Dwarf Planet Beyond Pluto—the Biggest in 20 Years
articles.description: The distant, icy celestial body could be our solar system's sixth dwarf planet.
articles.summary: The Rubin Observatory has discovered the largest dwarf planet candidate in 20 years—a distant icy celestial body that could be our solar system's sixth dwarf planet.

articles.title: Giant new dwarf planet discovered in our own solar system — hiding in plain sight
articles.description: A large object in the Kuiper Belt — a distant region of icy and rocky bodies past Neptune — appears to be a new candidate dwarf planet.
articles.summary: A giant new dwarf planet has been discovered in the Kuiper Belt beyond Neptune, revealing hidden worlds in our own solar system that were previously overlooked.

articles.title: NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope Captures Eerie Cat’s Head
articles.description: Intricate structures within the Cat’s Head Nebula are illuminated in this mid-infrared view from NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope released on Oct. 29, 2026. The distinctive “cat’s head” shape of the nebula was likely sculpted over time by the intense ultraviolet radiation and winds from massive stars in the Carina Nebula. As this stellar feedback […]
articles.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope reveals intricate structures within the Cat's Head Nebula in stunning mid-infrared detail.

articles.title: Ghostly Cat’s Head Nebula lurks within sight of Hubble and Webb
articles.description: The NASA/ESA Hubble and the NASA/ESA/CSA James Webb Space Telescopes recently stared at an eerie star-forming scene within the Carina Nebula, a massive gas and dust cloud located approximately 7500 light-years away from Earth. The two telescopes offer complementary views of the shadowy form, nicknamed the Cat’s Head Nebula, which reflects the 'magical'' process of star formation. Hubble’s visible-light view shows the cat as a dark, elongated dust pillar and hints of young forming stars, while Webb’s infrared-light imagery unveils many stars and other hidden details.
articles.summary: The Hubble and James Webb Space Telescopes collaborate to observe the Cat's Head Nebula, revealing an eerie star-forming region.

articles.title: MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.description:
Image:
			MMX lifts off to Mars’s moon Phobos
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission successfully launches toward Phobos, a groundbreaking exploration of Mars's mysterious moon.

articles.title: Celebrating BepiColombo, three words at a time
articles.description:
Video: 
			00:03:32
				
BepiColombo launched on 20 October 2018. This year, the anniversary is special. After eight years of travelling through the inner Solar System, the ESA/JAXA mission will arrive at Mercury on 9 December, 2026. To celebrate, mission team members were asked to describe BepiColombo in just three words.
Their answers capture the character of the mission and the people behind it. Complex, collaborative and transformative are among the words chosen, reflecting both the demanding journey to Mercury and the international teamwork that has made it possible. Together, their words offer a personal snapshot of BepiColombo as it approaches its long-awaited destination.
articles.summary: BepiColombo celebrates its milestone anniversary after eight years of its historic journey to study Mercury.

articles.title: Euclid discovers new comet
articles.description: The European Space Agency’s Euclid space telescope has discovered its first previously unknown comet, in images taken between 16 and 24 September 2026.
articles.summary: The European Space Agency's Euclid space telescope achieves a significant milestone by discovering its first previously unknown comet.

articles.title: Mars moon lander set to launch on 19 October
articles.description:
The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission is set to launch into space on a H3 rocket from the Tanegashima Space Center at 04:41 JST on 20 October 2026 (20:41 BST / 21:41 CEST on 19 October 2026). MMX will be the first mission to collect a sample from Mars’s moon Phobos and bring it back to Earth. 
MMX is led by the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA), in collaboration with the National Aeronautics and Space Administration (NASA), the French space agency (CNES), the German Aerospace Center (DLR) and the European Space Agency (ESA).
articles.summary: The Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission launches on an H3 rocket toward Mars's moon system for groundbreaking scientific research.

articles.title: Solar Orbiter tracks origin of mysterious magnetic switchbacks
articles.description: The European Space Agency-led Solar Orbiter spacecraft has flown through an S-shaped kink known as a ‘switchback’ in the solar wind’s magnetic field. By fingerprinting the elusive particles within the switchback, Solar Orbiter has traced its origin back to the Sun’s surface and revealed more about solar magnetism – the unruly instigator of dangerous solar storms.
articles.summary: ESA's Solar Orbiter has directly observed mysterious S-shaped magnetic switchbacks in the solar wind, advancing our understanding of solar magnetic phenomena. This breakthrough helps explain the complex dynamics of the solar atmosphere.

articles.title: Hera Probe Sees Asteroid Pair Separately for First Time
articles.description: Planetary defense is a growing concern among the scientific community, as efforts have been made to design and implement missions meant to deflect incoming threats to the Earth well in advance. In 2022, NASA intentionally collided the Double Asteroid Redirection test (DART) planetary defense spacecraft into the smaller asteroid of the binary asteroid, Didymos and Dimorphos, with the latter being the smaller one. While the goal was to ascertain if deflecting an asteroid is feasible, how did this influence the geological characteristics of Dimorphos, and what can it teach us about planetary defense missions?
articles.summary: The Hera probe has achieved the first separate observations of both asteroids in a binary system, marking a major advance in planetary defense technology. This mission demonstrates our growing capability to study and potentially deflect hazardous space objects.

articles.title: Queen's University Belfast Students Find Neptune's Elusive Trojan Asteroids
articles.description: Astronomers at Queen’s University Belfast have led an international team studying new solar system bodies near Neptune, helping to unravel the mysteries of our solar system’s evolution.
articles.summary: Queen's University Belfast astronomers have led an international team in discovering Neptune's elusive Trojan asteroids, revealing previously unknown bodies in our solar system. This discovery expands our knowledge of planetary orbital dynamics and asteroid populations.

articles.title: This Ancient Meteorite Hints at Mars' Warm, Wet Past
articles.description: Ancient Martian meteorites are like time-capsules from the planet's past. They're delivered to us by impacts that launch them into space, where some of them find their way to Earth. One recently discovered meteorite found in the Sahara desert adds weight to the idea that Mars was once warm and wet, and possibly habitable.
articles.summary: Ancient Martian meteorites provide compelling evidence that Mars once had a warm, wet climate capable of supporting life. These cosmic time-capsules offer invaluable insights into Mars' habitability and planetary evolution.

articles.title: It's a Ghost! No, It's a Stellar Crèche!
articles.description: Astronomers using the Chandra X-ray Observatory (CXO), the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) zeroed in on a wispy-looking region of the Carina Nebula and found a ghostly looking cloud seemingly floating in isolation among the other clouds of gas and dust. Just in time for Hallowe'en, although, it turns out that little cloud isn't the soul of departed stars. Instead, it's a region of the nebula has been actively engaged in creating batches of hot, young new stars.
articles.summary: The Chandra X-ray Observatory and James Webb Space Telescope have identified a wispy stellar nursery, revealing new insights into star formation. This discovery showcases the power of multi-wavelength astronomy in understanding cosmic processes.

articles.title: Figuring out where cosmic neutrinos come from is tricky—radio telescopes could help find 'ghost particles' origin
articles.description: Neutrinos are funny little particles that weigh almost nothing, making them one of the universe's most elusive building blocks. They can come from objects as mundane as bananas and as exotic as supernovas—the exploding death throes of massive stars. Most neutrinos stream through space and pass through the Earth without interacting with anything.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Radio telescopes offer a promising new approach to pinpointing the origin of elusive cosmic neutrinos, the universe's ghost particles. This advancement could revolutionize our ability to study high-energy astrophysical events.

articles.title: Tiny photonic chip links telescopes together to view the universe in 'astonishing' detail
articles.description: A tiny glass chip developed by researchers at Heriot-Watt University has linked two telescopes together to enable them to act as a single powerful instrument, marking an important step toward a new generation of astronomical technology.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: A groundbreaking photonic chip developed at Heriot-Watt University enables telescopes to be linked together for unprecedented detail in observing the universe. This technology represents a major leap forward in astronomical instrumentation and capabilities.

articles.title: A gamma-ray powerhouse's smoking gun? Gas trail points to microquasar jets
articles.description: In 2016, a binary star system emitting unusually strong gamma rays was discovered in our galactic neighborhood. Now, astronomers have found the smoking gun, or rather, a smoking trail of cool molecular gas that suggests jets emanating from a microquasar—one of the few known outside the Milky Way—are responsible.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Observations of a nearby microquasar's gas trail provide new evidence explaining its unusually powerful gamma-ray emissions. This discovery illuminates the physics of compact binary star systems and their energetic jets.

articles.title: NASA's Voyager 1 conserves power, resolves brief communications pause
articles.description: NASA's Voyager team is celebrating two recent developments with the Voyager 1 spacecraft: In September, they successfully completed a months-long effort to stretch the spacecraft's diminishing power supply. Then, on Oct. 20, an unexpected loss of communication with the spacecraft resolved itself after 48 hours, before the team sent commands to the spacecraft to troubleshoot the issue.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's Voyager 1 has successfully resolved a communications issue and implemented power conservation measures, continuing its historic mission beyond the heliopause. This achievement demonstrates the resilience of humanity's most distant spacecraft.

articles.title: JWST reveals a distant galaxy that may let most of its ionizing radiation escape
articles.description: Astronomers using the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) have found evidence that a distant, exceptionally blue galaxy may allow most of its ionizing radiation to escape into space. Known as EBG-1, the gravitationally lensed galaxy is seen at a redshift of 9.244, about 530 million years after the Big Bang. The paper was posted to the arXiv preprint server on Oct. 16.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: JWST has discovered a distant blue galaxy allowing most of its ionizing radiation to escape, offering new insights into galaxy formation and reionization. This finding advances our understanding of the early universe's evolution.

articles.title: NASA's TRACERS first results offer peek into violent magnetic process
articles.description: NASA's TRACERS (Tandem Reconnection and Cusp Electrodynamics Reconnaissance Satellites) mission has gathered its first clues to how space weather affects Earth's magnetic field. In a new paper published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Space Physics, researchers break down how these interactions work after analyzing initial observations from the first year of the mission.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: NASA's TRACERS mission has delivered its first results on magnetic reconnection, a violent process fundamental to understanding solar physics and space weather. This breakthrough enhances our ability to predict and understand cosmic magnetic phenomena.

articles.title: Extraterrestrial detection inspired by firefly communications could distinguish alien signals from pulsars
articles.description: When we think of extraterrestrial intelligence that might be out there among the stars, we tend to think of creatures not too unlike us, though maybe with gray skin, probably bald and with big black eyes. We focus on the familiar, humanoids. But there are many intelligent species on Earth that are nonhumanoid: dolphins, crows, pigs and—with swarm if not individual intelligence—ants and bees. The film "Arrival" conceived of hexapod beings more capable than humans and with a more sophisticated communication system.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: Researchers are developing new detection methods inspired by firefly communication that could help distinguish genuine extraterrestrial signals from natural pulsar emissions, advancing our search for intelligent life.

articles.title: Space station experiment to probe plant disease risks for future moon and Mars missions
articles.description: As NASA and its partners prepare for longer human missions beyond Earth, University of Florida researchers are investigating a challenge that could affect astronauts' ability to grow fresh food in space: plant disease.
articles.source: Space News - Space, Astronomy, Space Exploration
articles.summary: University of Florida scientists are conducting experiments on the International Space Station to understand plant disease risks for future human missions to the Moon and Mars, ensuring crew safety for deep space exploration.

articles.title: Astronauts just gave the International Space Station a powerful upgrade
articles.description: Two astronauts completed a 7-hour, 11-minute spacewalk to install a new solar array on the International Space Station, bringing NASA one step closer to a major power upgrade. Once the final array is installed on November 5, the station will have up to 30% more available power, supporting critical operations and its eventual controlled deorbit.
articles.summary: Two astronauts successfully completed a seven-hour spacewalk to install a powerful new solar array on the International Space Station, enhancing its capabilities for future missions.

articles.title: Physicists created a tiny universe and watched time emerge without a clock
articles.description: Scientists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that could help answer one of the biggest mysteries in physics: What is time, and where does it come from? Using 24,000 ultracold atoms, a University of Birmingham researcher built an isolated quantum system that repeatedly expands and contracts, mimicking the Big Bang and a possible Big Crunch. Remarkably, the experiment showed that time could emerge from changes happening inside the system, without relying on an external clock.
articles.summary: Scientists have created a miniature universe in the laboratory that demonstrates how time can emerge without a traditional clock, offering new insights into one of physics' greatest mysteries.

articles.title: Einstein's equations may explain the universe without dark energy
articles.description: Mathematicians have uncovered what they argue is a fundamental flaw in the standard model of the universe, potentially challenging the need for dark energy. Their calculations suggest that the mathematical framework used to describe cosmic expansion is inherently unstable and that the universe could accelerate naturally under Einstein's original theory of gravity. The findings also raise surprising questions about whether our location in the universe is as ordinary as scientists have long assumed.
articles.summary: Mathematicians have identified a potential fundamental flaw in the standard cosmological model, suggesting Einstein's equations alone may explain the universe without requiring dark energy.

articles.title: NASA discovers Jupiter’s invisible shield is more complex than Earth’s
articles.description: NASA’s Juno spacecraft has discovered that Jupiter uses a surprisingly complex system of powerful plasma waves and multiple shock regions to defend against the solar wind. The findings reveal major differences between Jupiter and Earth and could help scientists understand the enormous shock waves produced by exploding stars.
articles.summary: NASA's Juno spacecraft has revealed that Jupiter's magnetosphere is far more complex than Earth's, employing sophisticated plasma wave systems to create an invisible protective shield.

articles.title: A mysterious star system just 16 light-years away may be hiding habitable planets
articles.description: Astronomers have solved a 170-year-old planetary mystery in a nearby two-star system, discovering that a mysterious wobble was caused by stellar activity rather than a giant planet. Although Jupiter-sized worlds have been ruled out in key regions, smaller, potentially habitable planets could still be waiting to be discovered just 16 light-years from Earth.
articles.summary: Astronomers have solved a 170-year-old mystery in a nearby binary star system just 16 light-years away, discovering that it may harbor habitable planets.

articles.title: NASA’s Artemis I mission reveals surprising radiation levels near the Moon
articles.description: NASA’s Artemis I mission has revealed that cosmic radiation near the Moon is higher than in Earth orbit, but not by as much as scientists might expect. Tiny experimental detectors also uncovered surprising details about how radiation passes through the human body, offering valuable insights for future lunar exploration.
articles.summary: NASA's Artemis I mission has revealed new data about cosmic radiation levels near the Moon, providing crucial information for planning future crewed lunar missions.

articles.title: Possible dwarf planet discovered beyond Pluto
articles.description: Astronomers have found a large icy object beyond Pluto, dubbed 2026 ED138, that could become the solar system’s sixth dwarf planet Read Full Article at RT.com
articles.summary: Astronomers have discovered 2026 ED138, a large icy object beyond Pluto that could be our solar system's sixth dwarf planet, expanding our understanding of the distant reaches of our cosmic neighborhood.

articles.title: World's largest digital camera snaps new world beyond Pluto
articles.description: Space was so much simpler when I was a kid. Back in the 1980s, we still hoped to find habitable planets around every star. Nine planets orbited our own Sun. And “dwarf planet” sounded like a Saturday morning cartoon begging for its own toy line.Continue Readi…
articles.summary: The world's largest digital camera has captured images revealing new worlds beyond Pluto, advancing our exploration of the outer solar system.
